subject.title: Telegram: spooled-lane guard survives health-monitor channel restart — no escalation to a hard recovery boundary; only full gateway restart clears it

question: Should a wedged Telegram spool handler escalate to the shared supervised gateway-restart seam after a bounded TTL, or must recovery use a narrower handler-owned hard-cancellation boundary?
rationale: Both paths can restore delivery, but they differ materially in gateway-wide availability impact, plugin/core ownership, and behavior on unsupervised installations; source inspection cannot determine the intended product boundary.

options.title: Use supervised restart escalation
options.body: Accept the linked PR direction after proof that supervised restart drains queued Telegram updates, respects restart budgets, and does not silently claim recovery on unsupervised installations.

options.title: Require narrower hard cancellation
options.body: Keep the generic health surface unchanged and add an owner-specific termination boundary that proves the old handler cannot continue before releasing the lane.

recommendation.title: Use supervised restart escalation
recommendation.body: Accept the linked PR direction after proof that supervised restart drains queued Telegram updates, respects restart budgets, and does not silently claim recovery on unsupervised installations.

likelyOwner.reason: Their feature-history work established the stalled spool-handler and buffered replay ownership model that this boundary must preserve.
